findings.finding: The Q3 2026 numbers have been public since 07:30 ET today in the 10-Q, ahead of the scheduled after-close release. Revenue was $25.62M (+9% YoY but -3.5% QoQ from $26.55M) against a $27.1-27.3M consensus, a 5.8% miss. Diluted EPS was $0.16 against $0.24-0.25 (about $0.18 excluding $280k of restructuring). Implied adjusted EBITDA is about $3.2M (op income 2,655 + D&A about 250 + SBC about 57 + restructuring 280), against $3.8M in Q3 2025 and $3.67M in Q2 2026. Irwin, the growth leg, fell 8% QoQ ($14.1M to $13.0M); Legacy was flat QoQ at $12.6M (-24% YoY). The stock already trades -16% intraday on it, so for the close-to-close window only the residual reaches the trade: the wire release and call tonight carry the same numbers to a wider audience, with YoY headlines (revenue +9%, net income +71%) that read better than the consensus miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 also missed EPS badly ($0.09 vs a $0.27 consensus per Fintool) and the stock moved only -2.74% (baseline). Q2 2026: a revenue and EPS beat drew -3.5% in the days after on margin compression (webull/Simply Wall St, 2026-08-15), while the baseline records +9.06% on the day. Q4 2025 (2026-04-01): -14.79% when management flagged demand softness and declined guidance. So this name sells hardest on the forward commentary, not on the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, and in today's session, not in the window. Yahoo's intraday bar for 2026-11-16 opens at 7.65 against a prior close of 8.48, trades to 6.28 and sits at 7.12 on about 45k shares (4x the 20-day average). What is not priced is the second audience. The GlobeNewswire release and the call reach holders and screens that read wire copy rather than EDGAR, and the sell-side (Roth and others) will publish estimate cuts after the call, before tomorrow's open. If the residual were fully priced, today's bar would be closing at its low; instead it has bounced 13% off the low.

findings.finding: The 10-Q discloses a Q3 restructuring ($280k, mostly severance) that management expects to save about $1.2M a year in operating expense from Q4 2026. That is about 9% of trailing adjusted EBITDA of roughly $13.5M. Q4 2026 also laps Q4 2025, when management said broad-based demand softness began in mid-November. So tonight's call has two concrete positives to lead with on Q4: a cost cut already in the run-rate and an easy comparison.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Forward commentary is the line this name has moved most on: -14.79% on 2026-04-01 when management said demand softness had persisted and declined guidance. I found no instance of a cost-saving programme announced on a call to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: The savings figure sits in the 10-Q's MD&A, not in a headline. This morning's selling ran off the consensus miss (the EW banner). The call is where management quantifies the Q4 cost base and the comparison, and with no guidance the street has no Q4 number from the company to anchor on. If this were priced, today's intraday low would not have been bid back 13%. Conversely, the bounce off 6.28 may already be partly this.
findings.independence: The demand softness from mid-November 2025 (the easy comparison) comes from the Q4 2025 call coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/fitlife-brands-q4-earnings-call-highlights-2026-04-01/?.tsrc=rss, as relayed in search results). The restructuring figure is from the same 10-Q as findings 1 and 3.

findings.finding: I asked what the money buys: covenant relief, not a ramp. On 2026-10-30 FitLife amended its credit agreement, lifting maximum Senior Funded Debt/EBITDA from 2.50x (first tested at Q3 2026 under the original agreement) to 3.25x for Sept 30 and Dec 31 2026, stepping back down to 2.50x later, and setting a minimum fixed-charge coverage of 1.00x at Dec 2026 and Mar 2027. The 10-Q says the company was in compliance at Sept 30 'after giving effect to the Amended Credit Agreement', i.e. it needed the reset. Other balance-sheet facts from the 10-Q: cash $689k, revolver $4.8M drawn with $5.2M available, term loan $34.5M with $6.1M current, and nine-month operating cash flow $4.4M, down 38% from $7.2M. No 8-K was filed for the amendment, so this morning's 10-Q was its first disclosure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior covenant event at FitLife to compare against. Debt paydown was the positive management stressed on the Q2 2026 call ($8.6M repaid since the Irwin deal).
findings.why_not_priced: It was never in an 8-K (EDGAR submissions show no filing between the 2026-09-09 8-K and today's 10-Q: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001374328.json). It sits in the notes, while this morning's headline was the EPS miss. It reaches a wider audience on tonight's call Q&A and in the sell-side notes before tomorrow's open. The covenant first bites at a 3.25x maximum on Dec 31 2026, a quarter in which EBITDA is down YoY. If it were priced, I would expect the bid back from 6.28 to be absent.
findings.independence: The original 2.50x covenant tested from the Sept 30 2026 quarter is described in the credit-agreement filing surfaced by search (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001374328/000143774926016983/ex_963216.htm). Same 10-Q as findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: GNC, the Legacy wholesale customer the 10-Q names as the main cause of a 34% Legacy wholesale decline in Q3, is shrinking its US store base in 2026: Fast Company ran a list of GNC store closings dated 2026-08-21. That points to the Legacy wholesale drag carrying into Q4 and any commentary on the call. Net of the rest of the company: Legacy wholesale is about $3-4M a quarter (about 15% of revenue). Irwin wholesale (about $10M) and online are not GNC-dependent, so the net effect is small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The GNC decline has been disclosed in every 2026 quarter (Q2 release: Legacy wholesale -31% 'primarily GNC'). The stock fell around each print, but GNC was never isolated as the cause.
findings.why_not_priced: The closures are a proxy (a retailer's footprint, not FitLife's own Q4 number). The 34% Legacy wholesale drop is in the 10-Q and likely priced today. The forward read-through is what the call could confirm. Sized small because it is macro-to-company transmission the company has not quantified for Q4.
findings.independence: Fast Company, 2026-08-21, list of GNC store closings in 2026 (relayed in search snippets; the URL was not retrieved, so this is a proxy only). The Q2 2026 release (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-8-13-fitlife-brands-announces-second-quarter-2026-results) attributes the Legacy wholesale decline to GNC as well.

outside_window.finding: Covenant tests at 2026-12-31: maximum Senior Funded Debt/EBITDA 3.25x and minimum fixed-charge coverage 1.00x, stepping down to 2.50x and 1.25x in 2027, with Q3 adjusted EBITDA running about 15% below the prior year.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The 5- and 20-day run-up of -13% is almost entirely today's reaction to the 10-Q, so the findings mostly describe what the tape has already done. The residual lean is mildly negative (financing, GNC) against a positive call narrative (cost savings, easy Q4 comparison), which is why p_up sits at 47 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Two readings of one document are one finding: the Irwin -8% QoQ / management-credibility finding (-0.5) was merged into the reported-quarter finding, which moved from -0.5 to -0.6.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): I asked what the money buys. The answer is covenant relief with no ramp, so the covenant finding stays negative at -1.0.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the GNC finding was re-sized net of Irwin and online; it stays at -0.3.

Lesson 7: short interest looked up; not crowded on the latest reachable data, so no shrink for a squeeze. Lessons 6 and 8 changed nothing: the bar is two agreeing sources and the confirmed number is already public.
